_spec: BANZA assurance execution plan — strata, roles and the direction dependencies may point
_status: NON-NORMATIVE. Declares what each assurance command IS, so that composition is decided by role rather than by name. A generator called `foo-check` does not become read-only by its suffix.
_why: The assurance system became reflexive: a purity checker executed the aggregate assurance target, whose evidence collection reached the mutation runner, which invoked the purity proof again. That is a cycle, and it announced itself as a ten-minute timeout rather than as an error. Cycles are now rejected structurally, before anything runs.

M0.name: meta-engine semantics
M0.what: synthetic tests proving the engine semantics on fixtures it builds, and structural validation of the execution graph itself; neither executes repository-wide assurance

M1.name: graph and purity
M1.what: validates the execution graph is acyclic and that observational checks leave tracked state unchanged

M2.name: evidence collection
M2.what: executes registered property evidence and binds results to source and registry

M3.name: property and gate evaluation
M3.what: consumes registry, evidence and meta status; decides AG-0…AG-10

M4.name: repository falsification
M4.what: isolated-worktree mutation proofs; runs only after a green normal baseline

dependency_direction: M0 → M1 → M2 → M3 → M4. A later stratum may depend on an earlier one. An earlier stratum must never invoke a later one.

commands._why: structural validation over declarations only — it reads the plan and the Makefile, executes no repository evidence, and must run before anything else can be trusted to terminate

forbidden_edges.why: a purity or graph check that invokes the mutation runner is the cycle that produced the timeout
evidence collection must not launch the falsification phase it is evidence for
a meta check must not execute the aggregate whose members it inspects
synthetic semantics must not depend on repository evidence
